# Is the Model Telling the Truth?

For four weeks we have been glancing at residual plots and saying "nothing obviously wrong." This week each of those glances becomes a named assumption, with a diagnostic, a consequence when it fails, and something to do about it.

We work two examples on purpose. One is a model you already know (sleep, stress, and depression in the ASAP study) that passes with only a small caveat. The other is the Spotify model from Week 7, with an R² of .62, that breaks every rule until a single transformation fixes it. Both outcomes are normal. Most of the time, diagnostics take five minutes and one sentence in your write-up.

::: callout-note
## The sentence to watch for this week

Regression assumptions are claims about the **residuals**, not about your raw variables. A skewed predictor is fine. A skewed set of leftovers is worth a look.
:::
